meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_168_packages.json, and the full source text torah_168.txt. Because reference===168 has zero pre-existing bechina edges in torahData.js, there are no 'unassigned_dataset_nodes' to reconcile. All nodes in both proposed packages are new. The additions section below identifies every bechina-bearing concept from the source text with its proposed package assignment, source quote, and the explicit language that justifies the bechina classification. Torah #168 does not use the word 'בְּחִינַת' — it uses implicit verse-citation hermeneutic (citing a verse to identify a concept with a near-synonym) as its bechina-establishing technique.

additions.reason: The verse cited — 'לִפְנֵי שֶׁבֶר גָּאוֹן' (Proverbs 16:18) — uses 'גָּאוֹן' (arrogance/pride). The Rebbe cites this verse specifically to explain the phenomenon of 'גַּדְלוּת' (inflation of self). By this citation, גאוה IS the nature of גדלות in the same sense that a prooftext-word establishes a bechina-identity. The node 'גאוה' (pride/arrogance) is the conceptual referent of 'גאון' in the verse — the Rebbe's hermeneutic move is: the verse names this quality as גאון, I am calling it גדלות, therefore they share the same essential nature. Both גאוה and גדלות name the same spiritual reality: the swelling of self-regard that positions a person as great in their own eyes.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁבָּא לָאָדָם גַּדְלוּת, סִימָן שֶׁיָּבוֹא לוֹ צָרָה, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: לִפְנֵי שֶׁבֶר גָּאוֹן

additions.reason: גַּדְלוּת is the word the Rebbe opens with — 'כְּשֶׁבָּא לָאָדָם גַּדְלוּת'. It is the teaching's primary label for pride-as-inflation. The Rebbe uses it as the operative term whose nature is confirmed by the verse-citation of 'גָּאוֹן'. Dominant node of Package 1 (though גאוה is slightly more prominent as the canonical Hebrew term for pride).

The verse cited — 'וְלִפְנֵי כָבוֹד עֲנָוָה' (Proverbs 16:15) — uses 'עֲנָוָה' (humility). The Rebbe cites this verse specifically to explain the phenomenon of 'שָׁפָל' (being lowly). By this citation, ענוה IS the nature of שפלות — two names for the same spiritual quality of voluntary self-lowering. ענוה and שפלות share the essential nature: the orientation of smallness, non-inflation, receptiveness that makes space for divine honor to fill. The Rebbe treats them as bechina-equivalents through the same verse-citation hermeneutic as Package 1.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁהוּא שָׁפָל, סִימָן שֶׁיָּבוֹא לְכָבוֹד גָּדוֹל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וְלִפְנֵי כָבוֹד עֲנָוָה

additions.reason: שְׁפָלוּת is the word from the teaching's second sentence — 'כְּשֶׁהוּא שָׁפָל'. It is the Rebbe's operative label for the state of lowliness whose verse-name is 'עֲנָוָה'. 'שָׁפָל' (the adjective form, meaning 'lowly') gives rise to 'שְׁפָלוּת' (the noun form, 'lowliness'). Both forms appear in Breslov literature as a central positive virtue — שפלות in Likutay Moharan is the condition of the servant who experiences himself as nothing before God, which is the soil in which all genuine spiritual growth grows.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Appears in the verse 'לִפְנֵי שֶׁבֶר גָּאוֹן'. שבר is an eitza-consequence of גאוה/גדלות — it is what pride LEADS TO, not what pride IS. The Rebbe's teaching is 'pride is a SIGN that destruction will come' — the word 'סִימָן' establishes a directional signal relationship (eitza), not shared-nature equivalence (bechina). Excluded from packages. Would appear as an eitza edge: גאוה → שבר.

The teaching says pride is 'a sign that trouble will come' — 'סִימָן שֶׁיָּבוֹא לוֹ צָרָה'. צרה is the eitza-destination of the pride cluster, not a bechina-equivalent. Excluded from packages. Would appear as an eitza edge: גדלות → צרה.

The teaching says humility is 'a sign that great honor will come' — 'סִימָן שֶׁיָּבוֹא לְכָבוֹד גָּדוֹל'. כבוד is the eitza-destination of the humility cluster, not a bechina-equivalent. Humility does not SHARE the essential nature of honor — it signals and makes room for honor. Excluded from packages. Would appear as an eitza edge: ענוה → כבוד.

analysis_notes.note_on_bechina_language: Torah #168 uses no explicit bechina formula ('בְּחִינַת', 'הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', 'הוּא בְּחִינוֹת'). The bechina equivalences are established through the verse-citation hermeneutic: the Rebbe states a spiritual phenomenon using word A ('גדלות') and then cites a verse that describes the same phenomenon using word B ('גאון'). In standard Breslov exegesis this is treated as a definitional equation: the verse-word IS the concept-word. This is the same hermeneutic visible throughout Likutay Moharan (e.g., citing a verse with the word 'חן' to establish a concept as bechina-חן). Applied here: גדלות IS גאון (=גאוה); שפל IS ענוה.
analysis_notes.note_on_teaching_uniqueness: Torah #168 is exceptional in the Likutay Moharan corpus for being a pure two-sentence sign-teaching with no kabbalistic superstructure. It has the character of a concise practical-wisdom statement (similar to a Mishnaic aphorism or a proverb in its own right) rather than the elaborate multi-move teachings typical of the volume. The two bechina-pairs (גאוה/גדלות, ענוה/שפלות) are the minimal necessary vocabulary for a teaching about pride and humility as divine signals. The entire conceptual content is expressed in these two pairs and their four eitza connections (pride → trouble-sign, gaon → shever-consequence [from verse], humility → honor-sign, anavah → kavod-consequence [from verse]).
analysis_notes.note_on_good_evil_mirror: Torah #168 is one of the clearest examples in Likutay Moharan of the good/evil mirror structure (framework section 4). Package 1 (pride/גאוה = evil) and Package 2 (humility/ענוה = good) are exact structural mirrors: same syntactic template, same verse-chapter (Proverbs 16), adjacent verses (16:15 and 16:18), same divine-sign mechanism ('סִימָן'). The evil package signals its own destruction; the good package signals its own reward. The mirror is not merely thematic — it is the explicit organizing principle of the Torah's two-sentence structure.
